discussion_comments.comment_body: I fixed this in 54ee82110. Clearing a custom base URL now sends an explicit `baseUrl: null` reset through the live connection contract. Core rebuilds provider configuration after removing the stale custom URL, so LM Studio returns to its manifest default while an empty string remains a distinct literal value. Regression coverage exercises the custom-to-default transition and transport parsing.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Same failure mode, different consequence. This replaced `getProviderCollectionSync(...).provider.capabilities` with `config.providerAuth`, so when that's missing or doesn't match `config.provider` the capability check is skipped entirely. A catalog-declared OAuth or local-auth provider outside the hard-coded `OAUTH_MANAGED_PROVIDERS` set then falls through to the missing-API-key path and gets reported as missing a key it never reads.

Fair catch. Before this PR a `metadata: null` clear was encoded as `{}` and the daemon wiped the record; my rewrite sent a literal `null`, which `asPlainRecord` decodes as omitted, so the clear became a no-op. No desktop or CLI caller passes `metadata: null` over the hub today, but it was a semantic change this diff introduced, so restored the `{}` encoding in 3e428e6dc and added a test for it.
